title: Response contract for empty title or author
description: The sources require rejection with a clear message but state no status code.
system_choice: HTTP 400 with a body naming the failing field (title or author).

title: Response contract for missing id on removal
description: AC-002 requires the missing case to be reported without altering the list; no status is stated.
system_choice: HTTP 404; the list is unchanged. Successful removal returns 204.

title: Book identifier and ordering
description: The sources require insertion order but do not define identifiers.
system_choice: Integer autoincrement primary key; list ordered by id ascending.

title: Persistence and web stack selection
description: TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md names Python, Flask, SQLite, and pytest; the Foundation Contract uses app_server and persistence as package names.
system_choice: Flask app_server package via create_app and web_client; SQLite persistence package via open_database and db_session; pytest as the runner.

title: Terminal verification gate
description: The sources require one terminal full-suite gate. It is the story that depends on every other story.
system_choice: feature-test-runner is terminal; it runs sh bin/test.sh unfiltered with Suite: full.

title: Database location for create_app
description: No spec names a DSN. create_app() reads READINGLIST_DATABASE and defaults to data/app.db under the project root. Tests redirect it to a temp store via an autouse fixture. Acceptance checks that call web_client() outside pytest write to data/app.db. Is that acceptable, or should the default become a temp store?
system_choice: No spec names a DSN. create_app() reads READINGLIST_DATABASE and defaults to data/app.db under the project root. Tests redirect it to a temp store via an autouse fixture. Acceptance checks that call web_client() outside pytest write to data/app.db. Is that acceptable, or should the default become a temp store?

title: Trim before storing
description: Title and author are trimmed before storage and the trimmed values are returned, following DATABASE.md's non-empty-after-trimming rule. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: Title and author are trimmed before storage and the trimmed values are returned, following DATABASE.md's non-empty-after-trimming rule. Is that acceptable?

title: Ordering guarantee
description: The DATABASE spec says ascending id, but the shipped SELECT has no ORDER BY. I sort by id in list_books so ordering does not depend on the engine. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The DATABASE spec says ascending id, but the shipped SELECT has no ORDER BY. I sort by id in list_books so ordering does not depend on the engine. Is that acceptable?

title: 404 response body
description: The spec requires status 404 but no body. I return {"id": <requested id>} so the caller can see which id was missing, mirroring the 400 responses that name the offending field. Is that acceptable, or should the body be empty?
